classification.difficultyReason: Three reading tasks on a negative-stem plot: range across zero, an in-range count that excludes -18, and the mode among repeated leaves.

content.prompt: This data shows the midday temperatures at an Australian Antarctic station on 11 days.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the difference between the highest and lowest temperatures?

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many days had a temperature between $-16^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $6^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$?

answer.worked: The temperatures in this interval are $-15,-10,-10,-9,-4,2,5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. There are 7 days.
Stem $-1$ has two leaves $0$, so $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ occurs twice. Every other temperature occurs once.
a) $11-(-26)=37$. b) $-15,-10,-10,-9,-4,2,5$ gives 7 days. c) Two leaves $0$ on stem $-1$ give $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ twice.
